title: Conditions on Which a Household May Give Up a Protection Plan
content:
A household may give a Pass and Trip Protection plan up at any time.

**1. The free look period (no longer in force).** The clause "The premium comes back in full only where the
plan is given up no later than the free look period counted in calendar days from the day the plan was taken."
is no longer in force, and what the free look period does when a plan is given up inside it is not decided by
it. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every
day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the
resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is
used. The comparison is not-later-than and the boundary day itself satisfies it. The free look period each
plan carries remains the plan's own figure and remains valid.

**2. What comes back after the free look period (no longer in force).** The clause "After the free look period
the plan's cancellation basis decides what comes back: on the pro rata basis the premium is returned for the
days of cover still to come, worked out over the days between the date cover began and the date it was due to
end; on the no refund basis nothing comes back at all." is no longer in force, and what is returned on a plan
given up is not worked out on it. The refund basis each plan carries remains the plan's own figure and remains
valid.

**3. The cancellation fee (no longer in force).** The clause "The plan's cancellation fee is retained from
whatever comes back." is no longer in force, and the cancellation fee is not dealt with on it. The fee each
plan carries remains the plan's own figure and remains valid.

**4. A plan on which a claim has been paid.** A plan on which a claim has already been paid is never refunded
any premium, whatever its basis, because the cover has already answered for itself.

**5. The day cover ends.** Cover ends on the day the cancellation is recorded and not on the day the household
says they stopped wanting it.

**Point of judgement (hypothetical).** A household who says they decided in December to stop wanting the plan
and gives it up in February: cover stood until the day in February on which the giving up is recorded, and the
day they say they decided does not shorten it.

superseded_clauses: The premium comes back in full only where the plan is given up no later than the free look period counted in calendar days from the day the plan was taken.

After the free look period the plan's cancellation basis decides what comes back: on the pro rata basis the premium is returned for the days of cover still to come, worked out over the days between the date cover began and the date it was due to end; on the no refund basis nothing comes back at all.
The plan's cancellation fee is retained from whatever comes back.
